'''Burke:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} {{legend0|#584cde|70–80%}} | title = [[Governor of Wisconsin|Governor]] | before_election = [[Scott Walker (politician)|Scott Walker]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Scott Walker (politician)|Scott Walker]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) |turnout=54.5% ({{decrease}} 3.3%)}} {{ElectionsWI}} The '''2014 Wisconsin gubernatorial election''' took place on November 4, 2014, to determine the [[Governor of Wisconsin|governor]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Wisconsin|lieutenant governor]] of the [[U.S. state]] of [[Wisconsin]]. It occurred concurrently with [[2014 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] in other states, [[2014 United States House of Representatives elections|elections]] to the [[United States House of Representatives]], and various [[2014 United States elections#State elections|state]] and [[2014 United States elections#Local elections|local elections]]. This was one of nine Republican-held governorships up for election in a state that [[Barack Obama]] won in the [[2012 United States presidential election|2012 presidential election]]. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Scott Walker (politician)|Scott Walker]] won re-election to a second term in office, defeating [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] businesswoman and [[Madison Metropolitan School District|Madison school board]] member [[Mary Burke]] and two minor party candidates in the general election. Walker, who was elected [[2010 Wisconsin gubernatorial election|in 2010]], survived an attempted recall [[2012 Wisconsin gubernatorial recall election|in 2012]], the first governor in United States history to do so, defeating Democrat [[Tom Barrett (Wisconsin politician)|Tom Barrett]] both times. Wisconsin voters had elected a governor from a different political party than the sitting president in 27 of the last 31 elections since 1932; only once has a Democratic candidate been elected governor in Wisconsin in the last 18 contests when a Democrat was in the White House.{{cite web |url=http://editions.lib.umn.edu/smartpolitics/2013/08/23/scott-walkers-ticket-to-ride-o/ |title= Scott Walker's Ticket to Ride: Obama in the White House? |work=Smart Politics |first=Eric |last=Ostermeier |date= August 23, 2013}} Eleven of the last twelve Wisconsin governors, dating back to Republican [[Vernon Wallace Thomson]] in the late 1950s, had, unlike Burke, previously won an election to state government, the exception being Republican [[Lee S. Dreyfus]] in 1978.{{cite web |url=http://editions.lib.umn.edu/smartpolitics/2014/09/17/wisconsin-gubernatorial-pathwa/ |title= Wisconsin Gubernatorial Pathways: How Does Burke's Measure Up? |work=Smart Politics |first=Eric |last=Ostermeier |date= September 17, 2014}} The polling leading up to the election was very close, with no candidate clearly in the lead. The consensus among most analysts was that the race was either a tossup or leaning Republican.
